artboards.title: A · The lobby, with a roster

annotations.text:
Groups — one phone, three people.
Redrawn against the running game, not from memory: every avatar is the real drawn face from public/art.js, and A is built on the lobby the phone actually renders — the room-code receipt with its perforated edge, the .prow list, the segmented switch, the ? explainer row. The boards are generated by design/groups/build.js, so the art cannot drift from the game again.

A is 1000 tall on purpose: the real lobby scrolls, and groups adds a whole roster section to it.

Two arguments the boards are making. The huddle runs on its own 45-second clock and never borrows from the round clock — the giver is scored on a fraction of that clock, so time spent dithering would pay them. And the buzz asks which person said it (D), which is the one addition that keeps aiming at a person alive, makes a wrong shout cost one head instead of three, and gives E its second layer for free.

G is the one to check. If the cycle strip doesn't teach the bench rule at a glance, the rule is too complicated and should go back to plain round-robin.
